sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the south-west corner of the Scotch Plains and Fanwood area at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with the streets running roughly square to the page and north toward the upper right. Terrill Road forms the west side; a dash-dot line along it is the boundary between the City of Plainfield and Scotch Plains. Front Street crosses the top of the sheet from Terrill Road to Hunter Avenue, and Midway Avenue runs diagonally across the foot. Between them the cross streets are Farley, Grant and Hunter Avenues, with Hoe and Jackson Avenues entering from the north above Front Street, and 2nd Street, Rose Place, Edwin Place, Martin Place and Cicilia Place laid out in the blocks west of Farley Avenue. Weaver, Beverly Avenue and Forepaugh Avenue serve the south-east blocks. A dash-dot borough line crosses the lower third, separating the Township of Scotch Plains above from the Borough of Fanwood below. The sheet is thinly built. The large blocks 100, 119 and 125 are almost empty, with an apartment house at the top and scattered frame dwellings and stables; the Terrill Inn stands on 2nd Street near Terrill Road. Closer building is confined to the small frame dwellings along the east side of Terrill Road, with a macaroni factory and a stone or tile works near McCrea Place at the left edge, and to the lots along Farley Avenue and the streets east of it. Six-inch and twelve-inch water pipes are drawn along Front Street, Farley Avenue, Hunter Avenue and 2nd Street, with hydrants at the corners. A scale bar and the Sanborn compass appear on the sheet, and block numbers 100 to 125 and 136 to 146 are printed. Strips at the left edge belong to blocks continued on other sheets.
notes: Front is lettered without a suffix; today it is Front Street.
Weaver is lettered without a suffix; today it is Weaver Street.
2nd Street is East 2nd Street in OpenStreetMap.
Rose Place has no counterpart in the OpenStreetMap extract.
McCrea Place / Terrill Road was left out of the control: the modern node lies 9 m from the drawn junction.
Front Street / Farley Avenue and Front Street / Grant Avenue were detected but rejected (7 to 8 m off the fit).
100 ft. Southwest Scotch Plains toward Plainfield: Front St, Hunter Av, Farley Av, Grant Av, Cicilia Pl, Martin Pl.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the village centre of Scotch Plains west of Park Avenue, at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with the streets running roughly square to the page and north toward the upper right. Front Street crosses the upper third of the sheet from Hunter Avenue on the left to Park Avenue at the right edge, and 2nd Street runs across the middle on a slight rise from Hunter Avenue to Park Avenue. Park Avenue slants down the right side of the page, with Westfield Avenue, Bartlet Street and Grand Street entering from the right edge. The cross streets are Hunter, Willow, Myrtle, Sycamore and Flanders Avenues, with Senger Place and the short Luth street in the southern blocks, and Curtiss Avenue and Liberty near the foot. Willow Avenue and Myrtle Avenue jog where they cross Front Street. A dash-dot borough line crosses the foot of the sheet between the Township of Scotch Plains and the Borough of Fanwood. The northern blocks along Front Street hold the Plainfield Nursery with its greenhouses and storage sheds, the W. H. Lee Hotel with a bowling alley, and Frawery's Hotel near Park Avenue; the north-east corner has a row of small frame dwellings and shops on Front Street. Block 148, with the A. Cole Farm, is a large open tract with a farm group of barns and sheds, and block 149 near the foot is mostly vacant, with lot lines laid out. The south-west corner has a row of small frame dwellings along Hunter Avenue. Six-inch water pipes run along Front Street, Hunter Avenue and Park Avenue with hydrants at the corners. The compass rose and the oval Scotch Plains cartouche stand in the northern blocks, and the scale bar is at the foot.
notes: Front is lettered without a suffix; today it is Front Street.
2nd Street is East 2nd Street in OpenStreetMap; Bartlet Street is Bartle Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Martine Avenue at the foot is North Martine Avenue.
Luth is marked Arbitrary and is not in the OpenStreetMap extract; Curtiss Avenue is not in the extract either.
Liberty and Madison Avenue at the foot: the modern Hunter Avenue / Madison Avenue node lies about 27 m from the drawn Liberty junction, so Madison Avenue was left out of the control.
Willow Avenue and Myrtle Avenue are drawn offset on either side of Front Street; both crossings are in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft. Front St, Willow Av, Curtis Av, Terrill Rd area west of Park Av.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre of Scotch Plains village at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with Park Avenue running up the left side of the page and north toward the upper right. It reaches from Grand Street at the top to Portland Avenue at the foot, where a dash-dot borough line separates the Township of Scotch Plains from the Borough of Fanwood, and from Park Avenue on the west to Cook Avenue on the east. Bartle Avenue and Westfield Avenue cross the sheet between them, with Forest Road, Union Avenue, Stout Avenue and Montague Avenue as the cross streets, and Church Avenue near the bottom. Front Street and 2nd Street meet Park Avenue from the west at the sheet edge. The commercial core is the row of small brick and frame stores along the east side of Park Avenue between Front Street and Bartle Avenue, with a drug store, a stone dwelling and the fire house behind them, and the post office and a plumber's shop on the next block south. Public buildings include the Scotch Plains Memorial Parish House on Grand Street, the Scotch Plains Public School, a large brick building on Park Avenue south of Westfield Avenue, and All Saints Church (Episcopal) further down Park Avenue. The blocks north of Westfield Avenue are closely built with frame dwellings and stables; those to the south are large, mostly empty lots with scattered dwellings, and the south-east quarter of the sheet is almost blank. Six-inch water pipes are drawn along Park Avenue, Bartle Avenue and Westfield Avenue, with hydrants at the corners. Block numbers 113 to 116, 132 to 135 and 150 to 153 are printed in the blocks.
notes: Grand is lettered without a suffix; today it is Grand Street.
2nd Street at Park Avenue is East 2nd Street in OpenStreetMap; Martine Avenue at the foot is North Martine Avenue.
Front Street / Park Avenue was not detected (the junction is at the sheet edge).
100 ft. Pilot. Village centre: Park Av, Front St, Grand St, Bartle Av, Westfield Av, Church Av, Forest Rd, Union, Stout, Montague and Cook Avs, Portland Av at the foot (Fanwood borough line).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the northern part of Scotch Plains village at 100 feet to an inch. It is drawn with the streets running roughly square to the page, Park Avenue crossing near the foot and the sheet's north arrow pointing to the upper left, so that north lies toward the upper left of the page. Green Brook winds from the top left to the foot of the sheet through the west side, crossed by concrete bridges at Union Avenue and Park Avenue, and marks the township line; the sheet shows two small wooded islands in the stream. The main streets are Union Avenue across the upper middle, Park Avenue near the foot, and Mountain Avenue, also lettered (Springfield Av.), running down the right-hand blocks. Scotland, Cook Avenue, Montague Avenue, Stout Avenue and Forest Road cross it from the top, with Meadow, Stanbery Avenue, Valley Avenue and Prospect Avenue running from Union Avenue to Scotland. Grand runs down the right edge. The blocks between Meadow and Prospect are long lot strips with frame dwellings, a hay and grain store, an Italian club and a carpet weaving shop. The east blocks hold the Scotch Plains M. E. Church on Mountain Avenue, a cemetery and the Scotch Plains Baptist Church near the right edge, and an auto repair shop on Park Avenue. Block 93, in the centre, is almost blank. The west side across Green Brook has the Former (Old) Hat Factory beside the Park Avenue bridge and a few dwellings on the roads at Hess, where lots are marked arbitrary. The foot of the sheet beyond Park Avenue is largely open ground with scattered dwellings. Six-inch water pipes are drawn along most streets.
notes: Scotland, Meadow and Grand are lettered without a suffix; today they are Scotland Street, Meadow Street and Grand Street.
(Springfield Av.) is lettered in parentheses along Mountain Avenue as a second name.
Stanbery Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract; US 22 now runs near its line.
Hess is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The lettering TOWNSHIP LINE follows Green Brook.
The north arrow points to the upper left; the sheet is fitted at about -39 degrees.
100 ft. North of the centre: Grand St, Union Av, Mountain Av, Stout Av, Scotland, Green Brook along the west.

sheet-6-1.description: The lower and larger part of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch below a heavy dividing line, covers thinly built country on the east side of Scotch Plains. Westfield Avenue crosses the part from Cook Avenue at the left edge to Westfield Road; east of Westfield Road the same street is lettered Plainfield Avenue, with a six-inch water pipe marked as proposed. Westfield Road runs down the page from the dividing line to the foot of the sheet. North of the avenue lie the large undivided blocks 112 and 17, with a few dwellings and stables near Cook Avenue and a single house near Westfield Road; south of it a row of frame dwellings, numbered 613 to 646, lines the avenue, and the land behind is the open block 152 and the parcel numbered 18. Near the foot of the sheet are the buildings of the Watching View Farm: a dairy house with dwelling above, a corn crib and a group of poultry houses. Dwelling house hydrants and six-inch water pipes are marked along Westfield Avenue and Cook Avenue. Most of the part is blank paper, the drawn ground being confined to the frontages of the two roads. The upper part of the sheet, separated by the heavy line, shows another district north of Mountain Avenue.
notes: Plainfield Avenue east of Westfield Road is today part of Westfield Avenue in OpenStreetMap (the name changes about 800 m further east).
Placed from two junctions on Westfield Avenue only (Cook Avenue and Westfield Road): a two-point helmert, low confidence.
The farm name is lettered 'Watching View Farm' (presumably Watchung View).

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (lower, larger) Westfield Av (lettered Plainfield Av east of Westfield Rd) with Cook Av and Westfield Rd, Watching View Farm; part 2 (upper) Stanbery, Valley, Prospect and Mountain Avs between Scotland and Coles Av / Westfield Rd.

sheet-6-2.description: The upper part of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch above a heavy dividing line, covers the blocks north of Mountain Avenue on the north side of Scotch Plains village. Scotland runs along the left edge and Coles Avenue along the right, with Stanbery Avenue, Valley Avenue and Prospect Avenue crossing between them, and Mountain Avenue along the foot, where Westfield Road continues the line of Coles Avenue southward and a short stretch of Cook Avenue meets Mountain Avenue from the south. Blocks 87, 97, 98 and 99 are laid out in narrow numbered house lots; the blocks along Prospect Avenue and Mountain Avenue carry small frame dwellings, stables and a few tile-roofed and brick-veneered houses, while the blocks north of Valley Avenue are almost empty. East of Coles Avenue lies the large tract numbered 16 with a few scattered dwellings, and Mountain Avenue continues east across tract 17 with a six-inch water pipe. Hydrants are marked on Mountain Avenue. The title cartouche and scale note are in the upper right.
notes: Coles Avenue, north of Mountain Avenue, is today the northern part of Westfield Road; the modern Coles Avenue is a different street south of Mountain Avenue.
Scotland is lettered without a suffix; today it is Scotland Street.
Stanbery Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap; its line is near today's US 22.
Cook Avenue / Mountain Avenue was left out of the fit (5.2 m residual; the modern junction is about 8 m from the drawn one).

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (lower, larger) Westfield Av (lettered Plainfield Av east of Westfield Rd) with Cook Av and Westfield Rd, Watching View Farm; part 2 (upper) Stanbery, Valley, Prospect and Mountain Avs between Scotland and Coles Av / Westfield Rd.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the northern part of the Borough of Fanwood, from Portland Avenue and the borough line with Scotch Plains at the top to Watson Road at the foot, and from Willoughby Road on the west to Forest Road on the east. Martine Avenue, the continuation of Park Avenue, curves down the middle of the sheet. To its west Madison Avenue, Russell Road and the curving Midway Avenue and Midway Circle lay out a residential tract of narrow lots, with Paterson Road crossing the lower half; to its east Woodland Avenue and a curved Paterson Road lead to Forest Road. The district is suburban: scattered frame dwellings with private garages, several marked as built from plans, along Martine Avenue, Madison Avenue and Forest Road, and much of the ground still in open blocks (149, 157 to 166, 179, 181). A narrow row of lots above Madison Avenue belongs to Scotch Plains block 149. Six-inch water pipes and hydrants are marked on Martine Avenue, Russell Road and Forest Road. A separately framed inset of Glenside Park occupies the lower left corner and is not part of this placement. The title cartouche, the Fanwood heading and the scale note are at the upper right.
notes: Martine Avenue is North Martine Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Midway Circle is not in OpenStreetMap.
North Martine Avenue / Paterson Road was left out of the fit (6.5 m residual); the curved streets of this sheet leave residuals of 1 to 5 m.
The Glenside Park inset in the lower left corner (part 2) was not georeferenced: private roads only.

100 ft. Fanwood north of the railroad: Portland, Madison, Martine, Midway, Russell, Willoughby, Paterson, Woodland, Forest, Watson. Inset at bottom left: Glenside Park, 'Located 2 1/2 miles N. of Scotch Plains', private roads only; left unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Glenside Park, 2 1/2 miles north of Scotch Plains (private roads, brook) (no street junction; private roads only, outside the reference box; needs parcel corners or surviving drives identified on modern data).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the western edge of Fanwood at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with Terrill Road running down the left side of the page and north toward the upper right. A dash-dot line along Terrill Road marks the boundary between Plainfield on the west and Fanwood on the east. Paterson Road crosses the upper third in a sweeping curve from Terrill Road to Hunter Avenue, with Midway Place branching from it near the top. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs diagonally from the left edge to the lower right as a broad bundle of tracks, crossing Terrill Road on a wooden bridge, and divides the sheet. North of it North Avenue curves across from Terrill Road, with the long narrow lots of blocks 169 to 173 either side of the curving Elm, Oak and Farley Avenues and Watson Road. South of the railroad South Avenue follows the tracks, and La Grande Avenue crosses the foot with Farley, 5th and 6th Avenues laid out in the lots of blocks 193 and 194; 5th Avenue is marked not opened. The built-up part is thin: scattered frame dwellings on the lots along Paterson Road, North Avenue and Terrill Road, a garage with a light, electric and heating notice at the railroad, the Maple Tree Inn on Terrill Road, and a few buildings at the foot. Most of the platted lots between Elm Avenue and Farley Avenue are blank, as are blocks 183, 184 and 191. Twelve-inch and six-inch water pipes are drawn along Paterson Road, Hunter Avenue and North Avenue, with a 24-inch main along the west edge. The compass rose and the Scotch Plains cartouche are at the top right.
notes: The street at the foot left, lettered E. 7th St., is East 7th Street in OpenStreetMap; the Terrill Road / East 7th Street / La Grande Avenue junction is a single modern node.
Midway Place, Oak Avenue, 5th Avenue and 6th Avenue are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.

Hunter Avenue and Farley Avenue are drawn on curves that differ from today's lines: Hunter Avenue / Watson Road is about 21 m and Farley Avenue / North Avenue about 13 m from the drawn junctions, and Hunter Avenue / Paterson Road about 12 m, so those junctions were left out of the control.
5th Avenue is marked not opened.
The scan carries a library stamp across the lower right corner.
100 ft. Fanwood west: Martine Av, North Av, South Av, La Grande Av, CRR of NJ.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the centre of Fanwood around the Central Railroad of New Jersey station, at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with the streets running roughly square to the page and north toward the upper right. Patterson Road crosses the top, with Hunter Avenue, Willoughby Road and Russell Road curving down the left half and Watson Road sweeping across the upper middle to Martine Avenue, which runs from the top right of the sheet to the railroad. North Avenue curves along the north side of the railroad and South Avenue along the south; the C. R. R. of N. J. crosses the page as a broad bundle of tracks, with wooden bridges carrying North Avenue and Martine Avenue over it, and a passenger station and a siding curving into the yard between them. North of the line the blocks (174 to 178 and 180) are thinly built with frame dwellings, among them The Homestead, a boarding house, and the community hall and fire department building on Watson Road. Tillotson Road and Forest Road leave Martine Avenue to the right, enclosing the triangular block 186, and a street marked Wynn, arbitrary, runs south beside the post office. South of the railroad, blocks 195 to 199 are laid out with 5th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets running down to La Grande Avenue; 5th Street and 2nd Street are marked not opened. The industrial frontage is along South Avenue near the station: the Fanwood Lumber and Supply Co. with its lumber sheds, Hand Lumber and Supply Co., H. B. Potter Co. Inc., the Barrat Manufacturing Co. and a garage. Six-inch and twelve-inch water pipes run along Patterson Road, Hunter Avenue, Martine Avenue and South Avenue.
notes: Patterson Road is Paterson Road in OpenStreetMap; the spelling is as printed.
Martine Avenue is North Martine Avenue and South Martine Avenue in OpenStreetMap, either side of the railroad.
Wynn is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and is marked arbitrary on the sheet.
5th Street and 2nd Street are marked not opened; the modern 2nd Street and 5th Street lines match the drawn positions.
Watson Road / Willoughby Road and North Avenue / Tillotson Road were not detected.
100 ft. Fanwood centre and station: Martine Av, North and South Avs, Watson Rd, La Grande Av, CRR of NJ.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the eastern part of Fanwood at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with the streets turned so that north lies toward the upper right and the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the page as a broad bundle of tracks from the left edge to the lower right. North of the line, Forest Road runs down the left side, Tillotson Road leaves it toward the upper right, and North Avenue curves from Forest Road past the long narrow lots of the east blocks to the right edge. Midway Avenue crosses the upper right on a diagonal. The blocks (181, 188 and 166) hold a scatter of frame dwellings and are otherwise open, with a tile and a brick structure in the middle blocks. South of the railroad, South Avenue runs from the left edge down to a lens-shaped block 202 formed where Old Line South Avenue branches off; Locust Avenue lies beyond it to the right. Lagrande Avenue curves across the lower third with Laurel Place and Beech Avenue to its right and below, and block 206 and block 207 are platted in lots with no buildings. On the left, 1st Street runs down to Lagrande Avenue, with Wynn marked arbitrary in the upper-left blocks. The one large building is Scotch Plains Public School No. 4, a fireproof brick school with bearing walls, in block 201, near the Fanwood Cider Co. works and a few dwellings on 1st Street. Six-inch and twelve-inch water pipes are drawn along Forest Road, Tillotson Road, North Avenue and South Avenue. The right and lower parts are largely blank and mostly continue on other sheets.
notes: Lagrande Avenue is La Grande Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the spelling is as printed.
Old Line South Avenue is lettered along the former line of South Avenue; the OpenStreetMap extract has Old South Avenue East near it.
Wynn is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and is marked arbitrary.

The Midway Avenue / North Avenue junction at the right edge is not drawn clearly and was left out of the control; the part has 7 control points mostly in the west and top, so the east half rests on the fit.
La Grande Avenue / Laurel Place, Laurel Place / South Avenue and North Avenue / Tillotson Road were not detected.
100 ft. Fanwood east: North Av, South Av, Laurel Pl, Beech Av, Terrill Rd, CRR of NJ.
